summary: The statement and proof are correct. The section and conditional-quantile construction covers d = 1, positive-volume nonsmooth convex bodies, and the omission of zero weights. The measurable triangular substitution rule needs only the stated positive derivatives in each coordinate's own input, and its product telescopes to each body's volume. The arithmetic-geometric mean calculation yields the claimed multiway density cap with the stated normalization, support, and mean. The covariance argument uses exactly the uniform-volume covariance of K and proves both inequalities, including the zero-displacement and equality cases. Positive-volume fibers are convex bodies, convexity gives the required Minkowski containment, and the specialization preserves all centroids and covariance definitions. No errors or gaps were found.
